3 WEEK 1 PRINTER’S CORRECTION SIGNS Objective: This week, I will learn ➢ Meaning of correction signs ➢ identify proofreader’s signs; and ➢ demonstrate the use of proofreaders’ signs What are Correction Signs? Correction signs are signs that are made by editors and typesetters to mark corrections before a work goes for printing. Correction signs or marks can also be called proof reader’s marks are used when amendments have to be made in typewritten or handwritten work of which fair copy is to be typed. These marks indicate problems in the text and suggest solutions. Correction marks come in two ways; 1. Abbreviations 2. Abstract symbols Proof Reading This is the process whereby a good typist checks and carefully read the document typed to ensure its error free.

4 S/N Correction sign Meaning 1 Itals Change the selected text to italics. 2 rom Change the italic to roman/vertical type. 3 Caps, u.c. Change the selected text to capital letters. 4 l.c. Change the letter to lower case. 5 Trs (transpose) Change the position of text. 6 Stet Let the original text remain. 7 Run on Do not start a new paragraph. 8 # Give a space between two words. 9 Del Delete the text or word. 10 λ Add another word or letter at the point you have identified. 11 N.P. Begin a fresh paragraph at the point you have identified. 12 Close up Close up the word, e.g. Thro ugh to make it- through. 13 Sp- CAPS Spaced capitals, e.g. A N I M A L; to type the word separating the letters using two spaces each. 14 →│ Indent a paragraph.

24 WEEK 5 PAGE SETTING Objective: This week I will be able to: ➢ demonstrate how to set up a new page. ➢ choose correct alignment. ➢ produce a document. What are Margins? A margin is a space separating text or other elements from the edge of the paper. It is commonly adjusted through the page setup. Margins are spaces allowed at the borders of a document to make the text more attractive and easier to understand. Margins can be set at the top, bottom, left side and right side of page.

25 Page Alignment Page alignment determines the appearance and the orientation of the edges of a paragraph. Correct Page Alignment 1. Left Alignment: To left align means to begin each line from the same point on the left margin. 2. Right Alignment: To right align means setting up your document such that words or letters end at the same point on the right margin 3. Centre Alignment: To centre align means to present your document such that each line has some space on the right and on the left of the page. 4. Justify: When you justify a text, all the lines on a page or pages of the document will form a straight line on both the right and left sides.

26 Page Orientation The way your document appears after you have printed it on papers depends on the orientation you chose while inputting the text. Basically, there are two-page orientations, namely portrait and landscape.

Parts of a Memorandum 1. The heading which consists of your distribution list, who it is from, the date and subject;

30 To: Name and position of the reader From: Name and position of the writer Date: Date the memo is sent Subject: A phrase that focusses the reader’s attention on the subject for the memo. 2. A memorandum can be short or long depending on the message involved.

37 WEEK 8 OFFICE PROCEDURE OBJECTIVE: By the end of this week, I will be able to: 1. explain the meaning of office procedure 2. list the importance of office procedure 3. state and explain the procedures for making payment 4. state the procedures for making payments by cash, cheques and bank drafts. Meaning of Office Procedure There is no one definition of what office procedure means; however, every office has its own set of rules or a system of running its affairs. An office procedure can be defined as the sequence in which certain operations are carried out in respect of what is done., how it is done, who does it, when and where it is done in an organisation.

38 Importance of Office Procedure 1. It helps in the smooth running of the office, reduces delays and solves problems in the system 2. It helps work to be done faster 3. It helps to minimize and prevent fraud 4. It helps in the overall coordination of the various sections of the organization 5. It helps to reduce errors in the performance of duties. 6. It reduces general cost of operations. Procedures for Making Payments, Preparing Bills and Invoices Once an order is received, it immediately goes to the sales office personnel who records the date, fills in missing details, makes adjustments and complete calculations. When all vital facts are assembled, a customer’s bill or invoice is made out. Bills: A bill is a document issued by the person who renders service to cover the cost services provided to his customers. E.g. schools issue out bills to their students to show the amount of what they owe.

39 Invoices: These are documents raised in respect of buying and selling of goods. The seller usually raises an invoice which he sends to the buyer of his goods. Receipts: A receipt is a document issued to the buyer by the seller because of money paid for goods bought. There are many procedures used in speeding up the preparation of bills and invoices. These include: 1. The Computer 2. The Typewriter 3. The typewriter-Calculator Combination: While the regular typewriter takes care of the language part of the billing operation, the billing clerk maybe delayed in the calculations, unless it is done in another machine. The typewriter-calculator device was created for this purpose. 4. The Cash Register Adaptation: The cash register is essentially an adding machine with a cash drawer. It prints the figures on a sales slip instead of punching a tape. 5. The Photocopying Technique: Many small offices such as those pharmacists and doctors prepare monthly bills and statements of accounts simply by making a photocopy of the client’s or customer’s account card.

40 Procedures for Making Payments A. Cash: Naira and kobo are usually accepted as payment for goods. People offer cash to settle bills for goods and services such as books, newspapers, food items, etc. B. Cheque: A cheque is a written order to a bank to pay on demand a stated some of money to the name stated on the cheque. A cheque can be open or crossed cheque. It is open when it can be cashed over the counter at the bank. It is crossed with two parallel lines drawn across the payee’s name. It cannot be cashed over the counter. C. Automated Teller Machine (ATM): Cash can be withdrawn at any time of the day using an ATM card. Advantages of Using an ATM 1. Using an ATM is faster than going into the bank to withdraw cash. 2. ATMs have reduced the risks associated with carrying large amounts of cash to transact business. 3. ATM can be used after banking hours and at any time of the day. 4. ATM has reduced the cost of operation of banks and increased their profitability. Disadvantages of Using an ATM 1. ATM service is yet to reach most rural parts of Nigeria 2. Those who are illiterate may not be able to use an ATM card or machine. 3. The amount of money that can be withdrawn from an ATM machine is limited. 4. ATM has led to a reduction in workforce in the banking profession.

41 D. Point of Sale (POS) Machine: This is another modern-day device that helps customers carry out payments and other financial transactions at the point of sale. Advantages of a POS Machine 1. It eliminates the possibility of cash theft and fake currency. 2. It can be accessed at any time of the day. 3. It makes it easier to track sales Disadvantages of POS Machine 1. It encourages spontaneous buying by the cardholder. 2. Because a POS machine relies heavily on technology, it can bring a business to a standstill when it breaks down. 3. It takes a little more time to complete a transaction than when paying by cash. 4. It requires some training to operate a POS machine. E. Bank Draft: A bank draft is like a cheque drawn by the bank on itself. Since it is a cheque the bank draws on itself, it is automatically paid when presented at the bank. F. Bank Transfer: This is another bank instrument which money is transferred from one person to another through the bank.

42 Imprest Account A petty cash as we know, records small items of business expenses. The original amount given to the petty cashier is called is called an imprest or float. This method of keeping petty cash is known as an imprest system. There are some points to bear in mind when completing or preparing a receipt: 1. Write out the receipt carefully as you would a cheque. 2. Be careful to record the date, the amount and identification accurately ad legibly. 3. Use a pen because it is less likely to fade and much difficult to alter. 4.
